text: Geetha has a conjecture about integers, of the form for all x (P(x) implies there exists y Q(x, y)), where P is a statement about integers and Q is a statement about pairs of integers. Which of the following option(s) would imply Geetha's conjecture?
options: there exists x (P(x) and for all y Q(x, y))
for all x for all y Q(x, y)
there exists y for all x (P(x) implies Q(x, y))
there exists x (P(x) and there exists y Q(x, y))
solution: (B) makes Q true for every pair, so for any x with P(x) a y can be chosen. (C) gives one y that works for every x, so for each x the same y witnesses the existential: the order there exists y for all x is stronger than for all x there exists y. (A) and (D) only supply a witness for one particular x, which says nothing about the other integers that satisfy P.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page for GATE CS 2023 Q.16 with two independent published solutions
answer_evidence: The accepted solutions conclude (B) and (C), using for all x for all y Q implies the conjecture, and there exists y for all x R implies for all x there exists y R.
